## Natural history notes

A large rhinoceros beetle characterized by its smooth, dark brown to black body, strong digging legs, and horned males, which may have a prominent central horn and smaller side horns. In Florida, it is found mostly in sandy habitats such as coastal plains, scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, oak woodlands, and other areas with loose soil and decaying organic material. Adults are mostly active at night and may come to lights, while the larvae develop underground in soil or decomposing plant material, helping recycle nutrients and serving as prey for birds, mammals, and other insect-eating wildlife.
